meta.scope: Taiwan Batch 11 — USA / Taiwan / China triangular intersections. Explicitly defines the overlapping and opposing forces: semiconductor supply-chain dependence, US–Taiwan economic-security alignment, residual Taiwan–China commercial links, decoupling / friendshoring dynamics, AI-driven demand concentration, and the ‘silicon shield’ strategic logic. Meta-nodes and relational indicators written so the force layout can express the triangle geometrically.
meta.strategy_note: User request to further define the USA/Taiwan/Chinese intersections. This batch does not replace earlier clusters; it supplies the relational and intersection nodes that let the three poles (US economic-security, Taiwan semiconductor core, Chinese commercial residual) interact as a structured triangle rather than three separate blobs.

candidates.title: USA–Taiwan–China economic-security triangle (meta-node)
candidates.publisher: Derived from AIT–TECRO instruments, MAC, MOEA, US Commerce / USTR, and related official series
candidates.description: Integrating meta-node that situates Taiwan’s semiconductor and trade statistics inside the triangular relationship with the United States (deepening economic-security alignment, reshoring, preferential trade) and Mainland China (residual commercial interdependence, declining relative dependence, strategic competition). Designed so the force layout can treat the three poles as a single high-mass geometric object.
referenced_by: US–Taiwan ART / investment MOU / export-control nodes (Batch 8)
Semiconductor production, science-park and advanced-capacity nodes (Batches 7–8)
Military / navy and US FMS nodes (Batch 9)
candidates.notes: Highest-level relational node. Pulls the previously separate US-security, Chinese-commercial and Taiwan-chip clusters into an explicit triangle.

candidates.title: ‘Silicon shield’ / strategic semiconductor concentration logic
candidates.publisher: Derived from official Taiwan and US policy language, National Defense Report, and industrial statistics
candidates.description: Recurring strategic concept that Taiwan’s dominant share of advanced semiconductor manufacturing capacity functions as an asymmetric deterrent and as a source of interdependence with the United States and global technology economies. Continuously referenced in defence, industrial and diplomatic documents.
referenced_by: National Defense Report and economic-security documents
candidates.notes: Conceptual but heavily cited node that explains why the semiconductor cluster carries geopolitical weight inside the triangle.

candidates.title: US import share shift — Taiwan vs China (goods trade)
candidates.publisher: US Census / Commerce data as reported and analysed in Taiwan official and statistical releases
candidates.description: Statistical observation that, under recent tariff and demand conditions, US goods imports from Taiwan have at times exceeded those from China, while Taiwan’s export orientation has shifted markedly toward the United States (US share of Taiwan exports rising sharply). Documents a concrete re-orientation of trade flows inside the triangle.
referenced_by: Taiwan Customs trade statistics by partner
candidates.notes: High-frequency quantitative marker of the triangle’s commercial rebalancing. Direct edge between the US-preferential and China-decoupling poles.

candidates.title: Semiconductor supply-chain triad — design (US), manufacturing (Taiwan), residual materials / demand (China)
candidates.publisher: Derived from MOEA, NSTC, US Commerce and industry statistics cited officially
candidates.description: Structural description of the still-dominant pattern in which advanced design and EDA remain heavily US-centric, leading-edge manufacturing remains concentrated in Taiwan, and certain materials, mature-node capacity and end-demand retain significant Chinese weight. The triad is the industrial core of the larger economic-security triangle.
referenced_by: US–Taiwan reshoring and investment MOU nodes
candidates.notes: Industrial anatomy of the triangle. Makes the division of labour inside the semiconductor complex explicit for the force layout.

candidates.title: Decoupling / friendshoring indicators (Taiwan outward investment and production relocation)
candidates.publisher: Investment Commission / MOEA / survey-based and official relocation indicators
candidates.description: Statistics and survey-derived indicators of Taiwanese firms reducing relative exposure to Mainland China and expanding capacity in the United States, Southeast Asia and other locations. Captures the operational side of diversification inside the triangle.
referenced_by: US-bound semiconductor investment and reshoring statistics
New Southbound Policy and Southeast Asian investment series
candidates.notes: Dynamic process node. Links the stock of China exposure to the flow of new capacity toward the US and other partners.

candidates.title: AI / HPC demand concentration on Taiwan manufacturing
candidates.publisher: MOEA industrial statistics / science-park revenue / export-order series
candidates.description: Statistical and official commentary showing that the surge in AI-server, high-performance computing and advanced-packaging demand is disproportionately served by Taiwanese manufacturing capacity. This concentration intensifies both the commercial value and the strategic weight of the Taiwan pole inside the triangle.
candidates.notes: Demand-side amplifier of the silicon-shield logic. Explains recent extreme growth rates and the heightened geopolitical salience of the manufacturing pole.

candidates.title: Export-control and technology-security measures affecting the triangle
candidates.publisher: US Commerce / Taiwan MOEA / related agencies
candidates.description: Policy and statistical traces of US-led export controls on advanced semiconductors and manufacturing equipment, Taiwan’s alignment with those controls, and the resulting constraints on technology flows toward China. Forms the regulatory spine of the security side of the triangle.
referenced_by: Advanced-process capacity and equipment import statistics
Cross-strait technology and investment screening measures
candidates.notes: Regulatory edge that actively shapes the triangle by limiting certain China-directed flows while deepening US–Taiwan technology alignment.

candidates.title: Residual cross-strait intermediate-goods and supply-chain linkages
candidates.description: Statistics on the remaining intermediate-goods trade and supply-chain connections between Taiwan and Mainland China, even as final-assembly and new investment have shifted. Documents the incomplete nature of decoupling inside the triangle.
referenced_by: Cross-strait trade statistics and ECFA early-harvest data
candidates.notes: Prevents the China pole from being treated as fully severed. Captures the sticky intermediate linkages that still exist.

candidates.title: US–Taiwan security–economic nexus (arms sales + trade/investment instruments)
candidates.publisher: Derived from FMS notifications, AIT–TECRO agreements, and Taiwan defence and trade statistics
candidates.description: Relational node that binds the large and growing US arms-sales backlog to the parallel deepening of preferential trade, investment facilitation and supply-chain cooperation. Makes explicit that the security and economic tracks of the unofficial relationship reinforce each other inside the triangle.
referenced_by: US–Taiwan ART, 21st-Century Trade Initiative and investment MOUs
National Defense Report and defence-budget series
candidates.notes: Connects Batch 8 (economic-security) and Batch 9 (military) into a single US–Taiwan arm of the triangle.

candidates.title: Triangle tension / risk indicators (official and statistical proxies)
candidates.publisher: Derived from MAC, MND, CBC and related official releases
candidates.description: Composite statistical and policy indicators that track rising or falling tension inside the triangle — changes in trade and investment shares, special defence budgets, export-control intensity, people-exchange volumes, and official risk language in the National Defense Report and MAC assessments.
referenced_by: All major poles of the triangle (US economic-security, Chinese commercial, Taiwan semiconductor and defence)
candidates.notes: Dynamic monitoring node. Gives the force layout a way to express intensity of competition and interdependence rather than static positions only.
